items.title: ‘Like a knight hopping on chessboard’: What Maythil Radhakrishnan is to his readers
items.summary: It is hard to explain why a writer like Maythil Radhakrishnan, who qualifies to be a nerd, matters. Description falls short of the experience of reading him, and the most honest way to introduce his work is to put a book in someone's hands. Recently, when he was announced the winner of the Ezhuthachan Award, the highest honour given to a Malayalam writer by the Government of Keralam, Maythil’s readers were overjoyed and superlative in the praise of their beloved author. One sentiment that kept coming up was that he was grossly underrated; a writer belatedly recognised by a state for his literary genius. Maythil, 82, who wrote stories in his college years and had a stint in journalism, eventually chose the path of technology, as head of the computer department at a Norwegian shipping company and later, as senior technical writer with the Nest USA’s Chennai branch. Alongside, he wrote novels such as Sooryavamsam , Chuvanna Vidooshakarute Anchampathi and Hitchcockinte Itapetal ; poetry collections such as Bhoomiyeyum Maranatheyum Kurichu ; and, above all, short story collections like Naayakanmaar Shavapetakangalil and Dylan Thomasinte Panth .
